thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Nikkei Tumbles, China's Stock Market Finds Strength Following Tech Losses On Wall Street

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Nikkei Tumbles, China's Stock Market Finds Strength Following Tech Losses On Wall Street
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Apple component suppliers hit hard
Asian stock markets saw volatile trading Tuesday following Monday's rout, led by tech stocks, on Wall Street.
Every sector in Japan's stock market turned lower as the Nikkei dropped more than 2%. Investors were quick to react to the U.S. losses, especially among suppliers linked to Apple's (AAPL) iPhone. TDK (6762.TO) and Murata (6981.TO) were all down sharply. Meanwhile, SoftBank (9984.TO) rose 1.8%, making up an early 4% loss, following its after-the-bell update on the planned IPO for its Japanese mobile unit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/softbank-targets-20-billion-ipo-for-japanese-mobile-unit-2018-11-12-71035517). Japanese auto companies Toyota (7203.TO) and Honda (HMC) fell after reports hit saying the Trump administration is planning tariffs on auto imports.
Bucking an earlier sharper drop, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.6%, with energy stocks weak given oil's sharp reversal, with CNOOC (0883.HK) falling 3%.
Mainland China stocks fared better, with the Shanghai Composite managing a gain of nearly 1% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite up 1.6%. Still, iPhone component suppliers Secote Precision (603283.SH) and Luxshare (002475.SZ) both lower.
Benchmark indexes in South Korea and Taiwan dropped modestly, weighed down by tech names. Samsung (005930.SE) fell almost 2% and SK Hynix (000660.SE) plummeted 3.5%, while Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW) was off 1.7%.
Australia's ASX 200 closed down 1.8%, as energy and financial names dropped, and New Zealand stocks eased about 1%.
